findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled when the handler returns
findings.body: Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection start the legacy write in a goroutine via context.WithTimeoutCause on the incoming request context (lines 51, 110, 135, and 163). That child context is cancelled as soon as the apiserver finishes the request and cancels the parent, which is normally before the 10s timeout. The legacy write that mode 3 is supposed to perform as a safety copy therefore fails immediately with context canceled, so legacy storage silently diverges from unified storage.

findings.title: Legacy create/update replay the caller's object instead of the unified result
findings.body: After Storage.Create returns, the goroutine calls Legacy.Create with the same obj pointer the storage implementation just mutated (UID, resourceVersion, timestamps). Legacy.Update (line 139) likewise reuses the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of writing the object Storage.Update already produced. The previous mode 3 update path wrapped that result so both stores stored the same bytes. Legacy optimistic concurrency then sees the unified resourceVersion, rejects or no-ops the write, and the two stores diverge. Failures are not logged, only counted, so the mismatch is invisible.

findings.title: Storage failures and legacy delete-collection are recorded on the wrong metric series
findings.body: On Storage.Create failure the code calls recordLegacyDuration (line 45) instead of recordStorageDuration; Storage.Update failure does the same at line 129. Successful Delete records the object name as the kind label (line 106: recordStorageDuration(..., name, ...)) instead of options.Kind, so the kind cardinality is object names. The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration (line 166) rather than recordLegacyDuration, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to unified storage. Mode 3 dashboards and alerts will mis-attribute failures and cannot tell whether the safety write succeeded.

findings.title: Mode 3 unit tests mock the wrong store and never wait for the legacy goroutine
findings.body: The create/update/delete error cases set expectations on Legacy (or none on Storage) even though the implementation returns the Storage error and only then calls Legacy. An unmocked Storage.Create returns a nil error, so the wantErr cases do not exercise the path they name. Success cases start an unsynchronized goroutine that calls Legacy after the test function returns and never assert that the legacy call happened or that its error was recorded. These tests will flake or panic on the mock after the test ends and do not lock in the dual-write contract.

findings.title: Mode 3 playlist integration test reads legacy immediately after an async write
findings.body: The new mode 3 file/unified/etcd cases call doPlaylistTests, which creates, updates, and deletes through the Kubernetes API and then immediately lists and gets the same objects on the legacy /api/playlists endpoints (around lines 522-531 and getFromBothAPIs). Mode 3 only copies to legacy asynchronously and does not wait for that copy, so those assertions race the goroutine and will flake or fail even when the async write would eventually succeed.
